paper.title: Tracer Dispersion in a Self-Organized Critical System (the Oslo rice-pile model)

headline: Oslo rice-pile 1996 (1D stochastic SOC CA): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; L=256 tau=1.444 in [1.4,1.7], heavy-tailed (5.4 decades, max/median=76675x), <s> grows 32->256 over L=32->256

verdicts.gate: P1 Oslo exponent: discrete-MLE tau in [1.4, 1.7] at L=256 (kmin=1)
P2 genuinely critical in 1D at L=256: sizes span >= 2.0 decades AND max >= 100.0x median-nonzero
P3 cutoff scales with L: mean avalanche size <s> grows monotonically across L in {32,64,128,256}

extra.mechanism: 1D stochastic slope-relaxation cellular automaton: per-site critical slope z_c in {1,2} re-drawn on each toppling; drive at site 0; grains leave at the open right boundary. The stochastic re-drawn threshold is what makes the 1D pile genuinely critical (tau ~ 1.55), unlike the trivial deterministic 1D BTW pile.
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published SOC model; no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + lock-first discipline reproduce the Oslo 1D SOC avalanche exponent (tau ~ 1.55), its heavy-tailed criticality, and its finite-size cutoff scaling, and would catch an artifact

citations: Christensen, K., Corral, A., Frette, V., Feder, J. & Jossang, T. (1996). Tracer Dispersion in a Self-Organized Critical System. Physical Review Letters 77(1):107-110. doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.107.

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction graded against the Oslo 1D SOC signature (avalanche exponent tau, heavy-tailed distribution, finite-size cutoff scaling of <s>)
